text:
incidents-bot: ALERT: High streaming tail latency detected in eu-west-2. p99 streaming tail > 2s for last 10m. Affected endpoints: /v1/stream, websocket shard pool eu-west-2. Paging @Avery (oncall) and network team. https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streams/streaming-latency?orgId=1

pagerduty: Paging Avery (oncall) — incident triggered: STREAMING_TAIL_LATENCY_EU_WEST_2 (sev2)

Avery (oncall): On it. Acknowledging. Starting triage now — assigning Samira for networking assist.

Samira: I can join in 2m. Quick summary from console?

Avery (oncall): p95 jumped from ~110ms -> ~420ms. p99 from ~480ms -> ~2600ms. Streaming stalls (zero packets for >=100ms) rose to ~7% of streams. Downsampling from logs: 12% of requests in eu-west-2 have >1s additional handshake latency. Link to alert: https://alerts.redwood.example/alerts/1841000245

Jules: Noted. Any config rollouts in the last hour? I see a small rollout to routing-controller at 1840999000 but it was flagged green.

Marco: Running quick health checks on the NATs and VPC routers. Starting tcpdump on a sample streaming frontend host (fe-stream-021):
```
ssh admin@fe-stream-021 
sudo tcpdump -nn -i eth0 'tcp and (port 443)' -c 200 -w /tmp/stream-tcpdump.pcap
```

Priya: I'm pulling the streaming-tail traces from the trace backend for affected requests (trace IDs attached). Early glimpse shows many sessions with TLS handshake timeouts or extra handshake RTTs ~800-1200ms before first application data.

Samira: Running mtr/traceroute to upstream NAT egress gateway from fe-stream-021:
```
mtr -r -c 50 10.20.33.1
Host                              Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
fe-stream-021.example.local         0.0%    50    0.4   0.8   0.2   5.6   1.0
10.20.33.1 (vpc-egress-nat-1)      3.2%    50   12.0  15.8  11.9  45.1   6.4
10.20.34.5 (crosszone-router-a)    5.6%    50   20.4  22.7  19.9  58.0   8.1
10.200.5.6 (provider-peering)      0.0%    50   15.8  16.2  15.6  17.4   0.4
```
Looks like packet loss/loss spikes at the VPC egress NAT and cross-zone router hop.

Avery (oncall): That maps to the p99 handshake spikes. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion on NAT or a transient routing flap. Can we check NAT connection table sizes?

Samira: Querying NAT metrics: active connections spiked from 40k -> 210k in the last 12m, conn creation rate also high — ~9k/s. NAT CPU at 78%, connection table reach ~88% of capacity. Cloud provider API shows some NAT gateways in eu-west-2 reporting high retransmits.

network-eng-bot: NAT_CONN_COUNT: 210428, NAT_CONN_TABLE_UTIL: 88%, NAT_CPU: 78%, NAT_RETRANS: 12/s, ROUTER_PKT_DROP: 4.8% (10m)

Marco: I also see a small BGP flap between az-b and az-c around 1840999600 per provider logs — could have forced cross-AZ reroutes to overloaded NATs.

Jules: Any correlation with a customer deployment or traffic spike?

Priya: There was a viral load test from a partner system hitting streaming endpoints (burst of websocket connects) starting ~1840999800. That likely triggered connection surge.

Avery (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) divert new streaming sessions away from overloaded NATs via route table preference to alternate egress (fast failover); 2) temporarily scale additional NAT instances / enable more ephemeral ports if cloud allows; 3) enable per-connection keepalive tuning and backoff to reduce aggressive retry storms; 4) if streaming still bad, failover traffic to eu-west-1 as emergency fallback for hosted API. I'll apply step 1 and 2 now.

Samira: Applying route change to prefer nat-gateway-2 in az-a for fe-stream* subnets. Propagating.

Marco: Kicked autoscale for NAT pool; new NAT nodes requested (3) — cloud indicates provisioning ETA ~120s.

Avery (oncall): Rolling restart of a handful of frontend streamers to pick up new egress path (doing in waves to avoid disconnecting too many streams):
```
for host in fe-stream-021 fe-stream-022 fe-stream-023; do
  ssh admin@$host 'sudo systemctl restart stream-proxy && sleep 6'
done
```

Priya: After route change + NAT scale, initial metrics: p95 dropped to ~200ms, p99 down to ~900ms, streaming stalls down to ~2.1%. Good early signal.

Samira: NAT connection table now 43% after scale and route split. Retransmits trending down.

network-eng-bot: NAT_CONN_COUNT: 89,123, NAT_CONN_TABLE_UTIL: 43%, NAT_CPU: 32%, ROUTER_PKT_DROP: 0.9% (5m)

Jules: Any residual errors in TLS handshake logs?

Priya: TLS handshake latencies mostly normalized. A tiny tail remains for long-lived websocket reconnects that hit old routes and will drain over 10-15m.

Avery (oncall): I'm going to hand to Samira for next 30m to watch network and let autoscale stabilize. Samira — please own incident until I give final sign-off. I'm documenting steps in the incident board.

Samira: Taking over. Notes: cause = NAT capacity exhaustion triggered by traffic surge (partner load test) + transient routing flap that pushed traffic to overloaded NATs. Immediate mitigations applied: route preference, NAT autoscale, frontend restart waves.

Marco: Raising action item: put guardrails to limit abrupt connection bursts from external partners (rate-limits at edge LB) and add NAT table autoscale earlier.

Jules: Also recommended: add alert for NAT_CONN_TABLE_UTIL > 70% and synthetic websocket open tests to detect handshake tail early.

Priya: Customer impact summary for postmortem: - Time window: 1841000200 -> 1841003600 (~56m) - SLO breach: p95/p99 for streaming exceeded SLO for ~32m - Affected customers: hosted API EU region (approx 12% of requests experienced >1s extra tail latency), some live streaming customers saw transient stalls and reconnects.

Avery (oncall): Thank you team. I'm marking 'investigating -> mitigated' on the incident. Handing to Samira for monitoring and postmortem write-up. I'll join the postmortem review.

Samira: Accepted handoff. I'll run a deeper correlation with edge logs and provider support ticket (opening now). Provider ticket ID: CLOUD-97421.

network-eng-bot: OPEN_TICKET: CLOUD-97421 created with provider — referencing BGP flap and NAT overload events.

Priya: Adding remediation checklist for postmortem: 1) Edge rate-limit / token-bucket for websocket connect bursts; 2) NAT autoscale threshold reduction and automation to add ephemeral port pool if supported; 3) Expand synthetic streaming checks in eu-west-2 with strict latency alerts; 4) Run tabletop for partner onboarding traffic patterns.

Jules: I'll take ownership of #2 and coordinate with infra to validate autoscale triggers.

Avery (oncall): Final note before I sign off: no persistent data loss, best-effort for streaming reconnects worked, customer support notified for impacted tenants with suggested remediation (reconnect guidance). Will schedule postmortem with SLT stakeholders.

Samira: Monitoring continues. p99 now ~320ms and stable for last 10m. Closing the immediate paging loop.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT 1841000245 STATUS: mitigated. Duration: ~56m. Severity: Sev2. Primary cause: NAT capacity exhaustion + cross-AZ routing flap leading to packet loss and TLS handshake tail.

Avery (oncall): Handing incident to oncall rotation notes: see /incidents/1841000245 (doc) — include all logs, tcpdumps, grafana panels, and provider ticket. Back to normal ops. :white_check_mark:

Samira: I'll compile the raw artifacts and draft postmortem tomorrow. Leaving watches on until 1841007000.

Marco: Thanks everyone. Good triage and fast mitigation. :clap:
